newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai indices end up, Shenzhen mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai indices end up, Shenzhen mixed.

text.p: Shanghai share indices ended up on Tuesday, driven by bullish sentiment on the A share market, but Shenzhen indices finished mixed as investors took profits during the company reporting season, analysts said.
Shanghai's B share index added 0.331 point or 0.46 percent to 71.623 on volume of 18.5 million shares worth $9.4 million.
"Some domestic bargain hunting pushed the index up in the absence of foreign funds," one broker said.

Brokers said the index was likely to consolidate in the short term despite rises over the past few days with overseas investors unwilling to build positions in the company reporting season when results for most firms have yet to be released.
Toy maker Shanghai Haixin was the star on expectations of strong 1996 results, rising $0.036 or 6.54 percent to $0.586 on volume of 694,400 shares.

Real estate developer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development traded the most on follow-up buying triggered by institutional support, gaining $0.016 or 1.62 percent to $0.998 on volume of 2.7 million shares.

Shenzhen's B share index ended slightly down despite a strong debut by Wafangdian Bearing. It lost 0.86 points or 0.53 percent to 162.08 points on turnover of HK$172.8 million compared with Monday's HK$76.8 million.
"Wafangdian's performance sent positive signals to the market, but investors are holding their breath ahead of the flood of annual reports expected very soon," said one broker.
Only three out of the 44 B share companies listed in Shenzhen have made their results public, with the official April 30 deadline approaching.
Wafangdian, which debuted in Shenzhen on Tuesday, opened at HK$4.05 or 52.26 percent up on the issue price of HK$2.66.
It quickly hit an intraday high of HK$5.53 before profit-taking trimmed gains, traders said.
Wafangdian closed at HK$5.02, up HK$2.36 or 88.72 percent on its issue price as 18.6 million shares changed hands, making it the day's most active stock.
Livzon Pharmaceutical was the worst performer, losing HK$0.20 or 3.47 percent to end the day at HK$5.56, on volume of 312,900 shares.
Shanghai's A share index stayed on its steady bull course, closing up 6.418 points or 0.51 percent at 1,254.717 on turnover of 10.2 billion yuan against 12.3 billion yuan on Monday.
The SSE 30 blue-chip index closed up 41.312 points or 1.2 percent to 3,482.478 points.
Textile firm Shanghai Dragon Head was the star on talk of financial restructuring, up 0.74 yuan or a daily limit-up of 10 percent to 8.11 yuan on volume of 7.9 million shares.
Shenzhen's A share index gained 4.29 points or 0.97 percent to 445.15 points on turnover of 13.8 billion yuan.
